expected_behavior: regression for the --anchors JSON comma-split bug: the JSON export used to join tokens with `paste -sd, -` and let jq re-split on ",", so a single backticked literal containing an internal comma (`mvn clean install, then deploy`) was corrupted into two array entries

skills/one's description ('Use for `mvn clean install, then deploy` invocations when the user asks about releases.') names one multi-word token that itself contains a comma; skills/two exists only to give the ownership table a second skill, anchored on the unrelated token `prettier`
`validate-skills.sh --anchors` on this fixture must report {"one": ["mvn clean install, then deploy"], "two": ["prettier"]} — one token, not two

because ownership is counted on the whole (unsplit) token, one's multi-word token is correctly unique and already named in its own 'Use for `...`' trigger sentence, so neither NO-UNIQUE-ANCHOR, ANCHOR-NOT-STATED, nor ANCHOR-COLLISION may fire for either skill
